basis: Every pin states a demand a court makes, quotes the operative language that makes it, names the evidence that answers it, names the instrument gate that tests it, and states what it does not prove. A pin may not be quoted beyond its tier.

tiers.A: operative text read at source this session, URL and HTTP status recorded
tiers.B: confirmed at an official case index or as reported; full text not read
tiers.C: confirmed to exist; not read at source
tiers.UNVERIFIABLE-HERE: a probe was made and failed; not relied on

pins.demand: the account must be a 'statement' made by a 'declarant' before the hearsay bar can attach at all
pins.text: "Statement" means a person's oral assertion, written assertion, or nonverbal conduct, if the person intended it as an assertion. "Declarant" means the person who made the statement.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, rule text quoted verbatim
satisfied_by: the output itself plus the process record that produced it; there is no person to name, which is the point
pins.does_not_prove: not relevance, not authenticity, not reliability, not weight. 801 answers one question and answers nothing else; a proponent who stops here has cleared a threshold, not a case.

pins.demand: evidence sufficient to support a finding that the item is what the proponent claims it is
pins.text: To satisfy the requirement of authenticating or identifying an item of evidence, the proponent must produce evidence sufficient to support a finding that the item is what the proponent claims it is.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200
satisfied_by: a witness with knowledge (901(b)(1))
a process description with a measured accurate result (901(b)(9))
a 902(13) or 902(14) certification with pre-trial notice
pins.does_not_prove: the threshold is 'sufficient to support a finding', not proof; the opponent may still contest authenticity.

pins.demand: a description of the process or system, and a showing that it produces an accurate result
pins.text: Evidence About a Process or System. Evidence describing a process or system and showing that it produces an accurate result.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200
satisfied_by: a written process description naming version, inputs, transformations and outputs
a measured accurate result: a stated error rate, an evaluation, or a controlled comparison
the design record that shows the result was not tuned to this case
pins.does_not_prove: accuracy of the process is not accuracy of this output on these facts; a validated system can produce a wrong answer, and that is a weight question.

pins.demand: a qualified person's certification of the electronic process, with reasonable written pre-trial notice, where self-authentication is claimed
pins.text: (13) Certified Records Generated by an Electronic Process or System. A record generated by an electronic process or system that produces an accurate result, as shown by a certification of a qualified person that complies with the certification requirements of Rule 902(11) or (12). The proponent must also meet the notice requirements of Rule 902(11). (14) Certified Data Copied from an Electronic Device, Storage Medium, or File. Data copied from an electronic device, storage medium, or file, if authenticated by a process of digital identification, as shown by a certification of a qualified person ... The proponent also must meet the notice requirements of Rule 902 (11).
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, quoted verbatim including the notice sentence
satisfied_by: a signed certification by a named qualified person
written notice to the adverse party and availability of the record and certification for inspection
for 902(14), a process of digital identification (a hash or equivalent) recorded in the certification
pins.does_not_prove: a certification authenticates; it does not establish that the process is scientifically valid under 702, and it does not supply a witness the confrontation clause requires.

pins.demand: the original is required to prove content, and output readable by sight that accurately reflects the data is an original
pins.text: An original writing, recording, or photograph is required in order to prove its content unless these rules or a federal statute provides otherwise. ... For electronically stored information, "original" means any printout — or other output readable by sight — if it accurately reflects the information.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200 for both pages
satisfied_by: the output as generated, or a printout or rendering that accurately reflects the stored information
a showing of that accuracy (the same process record that answers 901(b)(9))
pins.does_not_prove: the best-evidence rule governs proof of content only; where the event is proved by other evidence, 1002 never engages.

pins.demand: five conditions of a record of a regularly conducted activity, shown by a custodian or a compliant certification
pins.text: A record of an act, event, condition, opinion, or diagnosis if: (A) the record was made at or near the time by — or from information transmitted by — someone with knowledge; (B) the record was kept in the course of a regularly conducted activity of a business, organization, occupation, or calling, whether or not for profit; (C) making the record was a regular practice of that activity; (D) all these conditions are shown by the testimony of the custodian or another qualified witness, or by a certification that complies with Rule 902(11) or (12) or with a statute permitting certification; and (E) the opponent does not show that the source of information or the method or circumstances of preparation indicate a lack of trustworthiness.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, all five subdivisions quoted
satisfied_by: the generated record with its timestamp and originating event
evidence that keeping such records is a regular practice, not a litigation artifact
a custodian's testimony or a 902(11) certification
an answer to the trustworthiness objection, anticipated
pins.does_not_prove: 803(6) does not make an opinion reliable; (A)'s 'someone with knowledge' is the weak joint for machine output and is the place an opponent will press.

pins.demand: a qualified witness, and a demonstration to the court that 702(a)-(d) are more likely than not satisfied
pins.cite: Fed. R. Evid. 702 (as amended eff. 1 Dec. 2023)
pins.text: A witness who is qualified as an expert by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education may testify in the form of an opinion or otherwise if the proponent demonstrates to the court that it is more likely than not that: (a) the expert's scientific, technical, or other specialized knowledge will help the trier of fact ...; (b) the testimony is based on sufficient facts or data; (c) the testimony is the product of reliable principles and methods; and (d) the expert's opinion reflects a reliable application of the principles and methods to the facts of the case.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200; text carries the 'more likely than not' formulation. Recorded defect, carried from the admissibility ledger 9.1: the same LII page listed 2011 in its amendment-history line while carrying the 2023 text.
satisfied_by: a named natural person with stated qualifications
a statement of the facts or data relied on (b)
a versioned method with an evaluation (c)
a showing of application to these facts (d)
pins.does_not_prove: that a machine may be the witness. 702's subject is 'a witness', and no subdivision supplies a route by which a model is sworn, qualified or cross-examined.

pins.demand: the confrontation right where a testimonial statement is offered and its author is unavailable
pins.text: Held: The State's use of Sylvia's statement violated the Confrontation Clause because, where testimonial statements are at issue, the only indicium of reliability sufficient to satisfy constitutional demands is confrontation.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200. Quoted from the Reporter's syllabus, which that page states 'constitutes no part of the opinion of the Court'; the opinion text was not read.
satisfied_by: a characterisation of the statement as non-testimonial, with the basis stated
or the declarant's availability and a prior opportunity to cross-examine
pins.does_not_prove: whether a given certificate is testimonial. That is a ruling on facts, not a reading of a rule, and the instrument says so in its output.

pins.demand: a certificate prepared for litigation is testimonial; a custodian's signature does not cure it
pins.text: Under Crawford, a witness's testimony against a defendant is inadmissible unless the witness appears at trial or, if the witness is unavailable, the defendant had a prior opportunity for cross-examination. ... The certificates here are affidavits, which fall within the 'core class of testimonial statements' covered by the Confrontation Clause.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, from the Reporter's syllabus (not the opinion text; the page says the syllabus is no part of the opinion)
satisfied_by: a record made in the ordinary course, before litigation was contemplated
or the analyst's live testimony
pins.does_not_prove: that every machine output is testimonial. The characterisation is fact-specific and the instrument reports it as a characterisation.

pins.demand: a surrogate who neither performed nor observed the work cannot satisfy confrontation by reading the report
pins.text: not quoted here; recorded at the admissibility ledger 3.6 tier and not re-read this session
pins.verified: carried from docs/ESQUIRE_ADMISSIBILITY_2026-11-04.md 3.6, and a fetch was attempted on 2026-11-04 and failed twice: /supct/html/09-10876.ZS.html returned HTTP 500 and /supremecourt/text/09-10876 returned HTTP 404. Tier B stands; the pin may not be quoted.
satisfied_by: the person who performed or observed the work, or a showing that the witness is not a surrogate
pins.does_not_prove: the plurality/merits split in related cases; this pin is used only for the surrogate point.

pins.demand: in an agency hearing: any oral or documentary evidence received, irrelevant or immaterial evidence excluded, the decision on the whole record, cross-examination for a full disclosure, and the transcript plus exhibits as the exclusive record
pins.text: Any oral or documentary evidence may be received, but the agency as a matter of policy shall provide for the exclusion of irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence. A sanction may not be imposed or rule or order issued except on consideration of the whole record or those parts thereof cited by a party and supported by and in accordance with the reliable, probative, and substantial evidence. ... A party is entitled to present his case or defense by oral or documentary evidence, to submit rebuttal evidence, and to conduct such cross-examination as may be required for a full and true disclosure of the facts. ... The transcript of testimony and exhibits, together with all papers and requests filed in the proceeding, constitutes the exclusive record for decision ...
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, subsections (d) and (e) quoted from the section text
satisfied_by: a record naming the standard the forum applies
disclosure of the output to the party
a recorded opportunity to respond and to cross-examine
a complete transcript and exhibit set
pins.does_not_prove: that the tribunal followed its own rule, or the vacatur standard for an award; neither is modelled.

pins.demand: a proprietary algorithmic score may be used at sentencing without a due-process violation on those facts, reported as requiring cautions and confining it to a non-determinative role
pins.text: not quoted; read at index level only. Reported: no due-process violation on the facts, with the opinion requiring warnings and confining the assessment to a non-determinative role.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 confirmed at a case index and by reported citation (Justia case page; vLex citation block: 371 Wis.2d 235, 881 N.W.2d 749, decided 13 July 2016). Full opinion not read.
satisfied_by: a record showing the score's role was disclosed and non-determinative
the cautions the opinion requires, stated in the record
pins.does_not_prove: that an undisclosed proprietary method satisfies 702, nor any federal holding. Tier B only; do not quote for a proposition wider than 'no due-process violation on those facts'.

pins.demand: the reviewer must hold authority to change the output; a nominal reviewer does not satisfy a human-review requirement
pins.text: A requirement that installs a human where a machine performed the work is a *human-of-record mandate*. It is not featherbedding, and calling it that is an error of law as well as of usage.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source in this repository (E-1 opening proposition quoted; E-5 read as a heading and cross-reference only)
satisfied_by: a named reviewer
a recorded grant of authority to alter or reject the output
the review record, including a decision to change nothing
pins.does_not_prove: that the review was adequate in substance; adequacy is a cross-examination fact, and the instrument grades authority, not diligence.

pins.demand: professional-conduct guidance on a lawyer's duty of candor and supervision when using generative output
pins.text: not read here
pins.verified: not fetched on 2026-11-04; carried as a citation already present in the instrument's G7 authority string and in the canon Part VII CONFIRMED list
satisfied_by: a cited opinion text, once fetched
pins.does_not_prove: anything, at this tier. Recorded so that the gate's authority string is not silently unpinned, and it may not be the sole support of any gate.

pins.demand: the statutory 'individual' means a natural person, so the machine is not the author or inventor
pins.authority: Thaler v. Perlmutter; canon Part VII
pins.text: not quoted; CONFIRMED at index level in the canon's own ledger, not re-fetched here
pins.verified: canon Part VII CONFIRMED list; not re-fetched 2026-11-04
satisfied_by: not an evidentiary artifact; this pin is context for E-11.8 and answers no gate
pins.does_not_prove: that personhood would help admissibility. E-11.8 argues the opposite, and the argument rests on P1's text rather than on this case.

pins.demand: an opinion resting on a citation that does not resolve is a sanctionable defect in the application of method
pins.authority: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., 678 F. Supp. 3d 443 (S.D.N.Y. 2023)
pins.text: not read here; tier C as recorded in the instrument's G4 authority string
pins.verified: confirmed to exist as recorded in tools/esquire_admissibility.py GATE_METADATA G4; not read at source 2026-11-04
satisfied_by: a citation-integrity check over every authority the output relies on, with the resolution result recorded
pins.does_not_prove: a general duty to verify citations of machine output; it is a sanctions decision on fabricated authorities, and G4 applies it narrowly.

pins.demand: the reliability inquiry is flexible and its factors are non-exhaustive
pins.authority: Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc., 509 U.S. 579 (1993)
pins.cite: 509 U.S. 579 (1993), as named in FRE 702's Committee Note
pins.text: Rule 702 has been amended in response to Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc., 509 U.S. 579 (1993), and to the many cases applying Daubert, including Kumho Tire Co. v. Carmichael, 119 S.Ct. 1167 (1999). [Committee Note on Rules-2000 Amendment, read at source]
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source inside the FRE 702 page's Committee Note, HTTP 200. The opinion itself was not read; the citation is verified, the holding is not quoted.
satisfied_by: a method evaluation that is not reduced to a checklist; a measured error rate may carry a novel method
pins.does_not_prove: that any particular factor is required, or the U.S. Reports citation commonly given for Kumho Tire, which was not read here.

pins.demand: the account must have a tendency to make a fact more or less probable, and that fact must be of consequence in determining the action
pins.text: Evidence is relevant if: (a) it has any tendency to make a fact more or less probable than it would be without the evidence; and (b) the fact is of consequence in determining the action.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, both subdivisions quoted
satisfied_by: a stated fact of consequence, named before the output is tendered
a stated chain from the output to that fact, in one sentence an opponent can attack
pins.does_not_prove: that the output is what it claims to be, or that it is reliable. Relevance is the threshold the other gates presuppose; passing 401 clears no other gate.

pins.demand: irrelevant evidence is not admissible, so a proffer that never names its fact of consequence fails before any other gate is reached
pins.text: Relevant evidence is admissible unless any of the following provides otherwise: the United States Constitution; a federal statute; these rules; or other rules prescribed by the Supreme Court. Irrelevant evidence is not admissible.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200, both sentences quoted
satisfied_by: the fact of consequence identified in the proffer, plus the rule or statute that would otherwise exclude it being answered
pins.does_not_prove: admissibility on the whole. 402 states the default and then defers to the Constitution, statutes, these rules and Supreme Court rules, which is precisely why the other ten gates exist.

pins.demand: the court may exclude relevant evidence whose probative value is substantially outweighed by unfair prejudice, confusion, misleading the jury, delay, waste of time, or cumulative presentation
pins.text: The court may exclude relevant evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by a danger of one or more of the following: unfair prejudice, confusing the issues, misleading the jury, undue delay, wasting time, or needlessly presenting cumulative evidence.
pins.verified: 2026-11-04 read at source, HTTP 200
satisfied_by: an answer, stated in the proffer, to the confusion and misleading-the-jury risks that a machine's confident register creates
pins.does_not_prove: that the balance goes the proponent's way. 403 commits the balance to the court, and the instrument may only report whether the proffer addressed it.

declared_gaps.title: Relevance and conditional relevance
declared_gaps.status: declared, not implemented: no gate in tools/esquire_admissibility.py tests relevance
declared_gaps.measured: grep -E "\b(401|402|403|104)\b" tools/esquire_admissibility.py returns zero matches on 2026-11-04
declared_gaps.why: A proffer can be authenticated, reliable, non-hearsay and still excluded: 402 excludes irrelevant evidence and 403 excludes relevant evidence whose probative value is substantially outweighed. The ten existing gates all presuppose a fact of consequence that none of them names.
declared_gaps.conditional_relevance: Machine output is the textbook case of conditional relevance: the output means something only if the input was what it claims to be. FRE 401's Committee Note routes that question to Rules 104(b) and 901, which is why G11 must be specified together with G5 rather than as a free-standing text check.
